checks.title: journald has a size cap
checks.rationale: Without SystemMaxUse the journal may use 10 percent of the filesystem, up to 4G. On a small VPS that is a large share of the disk, and a log flood can fill it.
checks.fix: Add a drop-in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/size.conf with `[Journal]` and `SystemMaxUse=1G`, then restart systemd-journald.

checks.title: Proxy access logs are rotated
checks.rationale: A reverse proxy access log grows with traffic and is never trimmed by the proxy itself. A log over 1 GiB with no logrotate rule is a future full disk. Only the usual /var/log locations of nginx, Caddy, Traefik, Apache and HAProxy are inspected; container logs are not.
checks.fix: Add a logrotate rule (use copytruncate when the proxy cannot reopen its log).
checks.breaks: copytruncate can lose a few lines written during the copy.

checks.title: Journal disk use
checks.rationale: Shows how much disk the journal uses now so it can be compared with the cap in LOG-001.

checks.title: A metrics agent is present
checks.rationale: Without metrics and an alert for disk and SSH logins you find out about problems from users. Informational: the usual agents (node exporter, Alloy, Netdata, Telegraf, Zabbix, Datadog) are looked for; agents that run as containers or in a PaaS are not detected.
checks.fix: Add monitoring with an alert for disk usage and SSH logins.

checks.title: The journal survives a reboot
checks.rationale: A volatile journal lives in /run and is erased at every reboot, including the reboot after a compromise or a crash, which is when the logs are needed. Persistent when Storage=persistent or Storage=auto with /var/log/journal present.
checks.fix: Create /var/log/journal (or set Storage=persistent in a drop-in) and restart systemd-journald.
checks.breaks: Logs then use disk space; set a cap (LOG-001).
